entries.proposition: The model is a whole-body Elovl1 knockout rescued in the epidermis only by a transgene; brain Elovl1 mRNA is near the detection limit. WWOX is not in the paper.
entries.snippet: The Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice, which are deficient in Elovl1 throughout the body except the epidermis, harbor the transgene Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) expressing 3×FLAG‐tagged ELOVL1 under the control of the epidermis‐specific human IVL (involucrin) promoter.

entries.proposition: Lipid analyses use three animals per genotype.
entries.snippet: Lipids were extracted from the brains of control (n = 3) and Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) (n = 3) mice, and GalCer (C), 2‐OH GalCer (D), sulfatide (E), 2‐OH sulfatide (F), sphingomyelin (G), and ceramide (H) species were analyzed by LC‐MS/MS.

entries.proposition: Whole-brain GalCer species of 24 or more carbons are almost undetectable in the knockout while C22:1 and shorter species rise; total GalCer and 2-OH GalCer are reduced by 39 and 34 percent.
entries.snippet: Consistent with the results of the TLC analysis, the total levels of GalCer and 2‐OH GalCer were reduced by 39% and 34%, respectively, in Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice relative to control mice.

entries.proposition: Total sphingomyelin and total ceramide are comparable between genotypes (the text separately says total sulfatide did not differ significantly).
entries.snippet: The total levels of sphingomyelin and ceramide were comparable between control and Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice.

entries.proposition: Ugt8a mRNA is 38 percent lower in the knockout brain; the authors cannot say how Elovl1 affects Ugt8a.
entries.snippet: There was a significant reduction in the mRNA levels of Ugt8a in Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice of 38% relative to control mice, while the levels of Cers2 and Fa2h were unchanged (Figure 2A–C).

entries.proposition: Electron microscopy is done only at 13 months, counting 96 and 73 axons in 13 fields; the number of animals is not stated in the legend.
entries.snippet: Average diameters ± SD of myelinated axons: n = 96 [Elovl1 +/+ Tg(IVL‐Elovl1)] and n = 73 [Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1)] total axons counted in 13 different fields of view.

entries.proposition: Myelin is thinner only in the smallest (below 0.4 um) and the largest (1.6 um or more) axons, the latter more severely.
entries.snippet: The thickness of myelin increased in proportion to axon diameter in control mice (Figure 3C); however, in Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice such proportionality was less obvious, and the myelin was significantly thinner in axons with diameters of <0.4 µm or ≥1.6 µm, the latter being more severely affected (Figure 3A, C).

entries.proposition: Only 22 of an expected 66 knockout mice were genotyped at three weeks, and two more died of startle epilepsy by eight weeks.
entries.snippet: There were 22 Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice, which was one‐third of the expected number of 66 (= 265/4) based on the Mendelian ratio.

entries.proposition: Startle epilepsy is recorded as a cause of death in two knockout mice; the cause of the early loss is stated as unclear.
entries.snippet: Three more of these mice were lost by the age of eight weeks, and two of them died from startle epilepsy.

entries.proposition: On the balance beam the text reports no difference on the wide beam and slower travel and more paw slips on the narrow beam.
entries.snippet: On the wide beam, there were no significant differences between control and Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice; however, on the narrow beam, Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice moved significantly more slowly and exhibited more paw slips (Figure 4K, L).

entries.proposition: PANEL READING, Figure 4K-N. 4L paw slips: the printed P for the genotype effect is .0199 on the wide beam and .0184 on the narrow beam, so the wide-beam slips also pass .05 although the text reports no wide-beam difference (both groups are near zero slips on the wide beam); 4K moving speed on the narrow beam P = .0252; 4N startle amplitude about 5.5 versus 3.3 at 120 dB (two asterisks), equal at 110 dB and below; n = 12 versus 10 to 11.

entries.proposition: The authors read the pattern as myelin thinning in a subset of axons without axonal abnormality and suggest an oligodendrocyte-autonomous defect in patients.
entries.snippet: Thus, the hypomyelination in patients with the ELOVL1 mutation may be caused by autonomous cellular defects in oligodendrocytes.

entries.proposition: The authors say the mouse motor deficit is mild with no paraplegia and that the species difference may reflect the degree of hypomyelination or axon length.
entries.snippet: This difference in the extent of motor dysfunction between human and mouse may result from the degree of hypomyelination.

entries.proposition: Retinal and corneal histology is normal at 16 weeks.
entries.snippet: These results suggest the absence of ocular abnormalities in Elovl1 −/− Tg(IVL‐Elovl1) mice.
